chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhūr, from Muʿammar ibn Khallād, who said:

I heard Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm saying to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: “Indeed, my son has heaviness in his tongue, so I will send him to you tomorrow, that you may wipe over his head and supplicate for him, for he is your mawla.” So he said: “He is the mawla of Abū Jaʿfar, so send him to him tomorrow.”

key_terms.تَدْعُوَ: you supplicate; to make du'a for him
key_terms.تَمْسَحُ: you wipe; referring to wiping over the child’s head
key_terms.ثِقْلٌ: heaviness; here, difficulty or impediment in speech
key_terms.لِلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام, the one being addressed for du'a
key_terms.مَوْلَاكَ: your mawla; here indicating affiliation and wilayah
key_terms.مَوْلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: the mawla of Abū Jaʿfar; indicating relation to and authority of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام indicate the authority of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام in al-Kāfī?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a man asking Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام to pray for his son who had difficulty with speech. The Imam عليه السلام directs him instead to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, indicating his spiritual authority and standing.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Jamhour, from Moammar Bin Khallad who said,

‘I heard Ismail Bin Ibrahim saying to Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘My son has heaviness in his tongue, so I would be sending him to you<sup>asws</sup> tomorrow for you<sup>asws</sup> to wipe upon his head and supplicate for him, for he is in your<sup>asws</sup> Wilayah’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He is in the Wilayah of Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> (9<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) therefore send him to him<sup>asws</sup> tomorrow’.
en.sarwar: 11. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Jumhur from Mu‘mmar ibn Khallad who has said the following.

“I heard ’Isma‘il ibn Ibrahim say to al-rida (a.s.), ‘My son feels heaviness in his tongue. I intend to sent him tomorrow to you. Pass you your hand over his head and pray for him. He is your Mawla (slave).’” The Imam (a.s.) said, “He is a Mawla (slave) of abu Ja’far (a.s.). send him tomorrow to him (abu Ja‘far (a.s.).”
